sections.h2: What should a Charlotte County property owner know first?
sections.html:
Charlotte County's tax collector mails one combined notice each year, and the county property appraiser sets the values behind it. Taxes are collected in arrears for the calendar year, so a bill dated November covers the year that just ended.

The collector's office describes the bill as a mix of ad valorem taxes, which follow value, and non-ad valorem assessments, which follow factors such as square footage or number of units. Stormwater, fire and rescue and solid waste are examples it names. The Board of County Commissioners, the School Board, city commissioners and other authorities set the millage rates, and the appraiser does not.

Census QuickFacts shows 217,212 residents on July 1, 2025, with 40.9% aged 65 or over and 83.8% owner-occupied housing. The county has 131,960 housing units, 681.12 square miles of land and a median owner-occupied value of $328,900 for 2020 to 2024. Building permits totaled 3,015 in 2025.

sections.h2: Which Charlotte County offices handle which part of the bill?
sections.html:
The property appraiser values the parcel and approves exemptions, the tax collector bills and collects, and the clerk of the circuit court runs tax deed sales.

  • Property appraiser: values, exemptions and homestead applications, phone (941) 743-1593 for exemption questions on a notice and (941) 743-1498 for assessed value questions.
  • Tax collector: bills, discounts, installment plans and delinquent taxes, phone (941) 743-1350.
  • Clerk of the circuit court: online tax deed sales, phone (941) 637-2130.

The tax collector's page lists its mailing address as 18500 Murdock Circle, Port Charlotte, FL 33948, which is also where installment applications are sent. If you get a bill for property you no longer own, forward it to the new owner or return it to the tax collector.

sections.h2: When are Charlotte County property taxes due and what are the discounts?
sections.html:
Statements go out on or before November 1, and the discount is 4% in November, 3% in December, 2% in January and 1% in February.

Charlotte County tax collector schedule for real estate taxes
ItemAs the collector states it
Statements mailedOn or before November 1
Discounts4% November, 3% December, 2% January, 1% February
DelinquentApril 1, with 3% interest plus advertising costs
Installment eligibilityEstimated tax over $100
Installment paymentsJune 30 (6% off), September 30 (4.5%), December 31 (3%), March 31 (none)
Certificate saleOn or before June 1, bidding down from 18%

An escrow lender normally pays the bill. If yours does, the mortgage company should request the bill, and you receive an informational copy.

sections.h2: How does the installment plan work in Charlotte County?
sections.html:
You apply to the tax collector before May 1, and the first payment is due no later than June 30.

Missing that first payment cancels your participation and the full tax is due by March 31. Once the first payment is made, you are in the program for the full year, and the collector says enrolled taxpayers are re-enrolled automatically. To leave the plan, the office says to disregard the June bill, after which a November bill arrives for the gross amount. Any amount unpaid on April 1 is handled as a delinquent bill.

The first two installments are each a quarter of the estimated tax. The third and fourth add equal shares of any adjustment to actual tax liability, which can move the final two bills up or down.

sections.h2: What happens if Charlotte County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid real estate tax turns delinquent on April 1, then goes to a tax certificate sale held on or before June 1.

The collector advertises delinquent parcels once a week for three consecutive weeks, and advertising and collection fees are added. The sale is a reverse auction on the interest rate starting at 18%, and the lowest bidder gets the certificate, a first lien. A certificate is valid for seven years. After two years from the delinquency date, the holder may apply for a tax deed, and the clerk runs the sale online.

  • Delinquent taxes must be paid in certified funds: cashier's check, money order or cash.
  • The starting bid at a tax deed sale adds a $75.00 collector fee, a $150.00 ownership report, a $60.00 clerk fee and a $59.00 web fee to taxes, interest and half the assessed value.
  • You can stop a sale by paying all taxes, costs and interest before the deed is issued.

sections.h2: How do homestead, Save Our Homes and the March 1 deadline apply here?
sections.html:
Apply with the county property appraiser by March 1 of the year you want the benefit, with the home as your permanent residence on January 1.

The state exemption is up to $50,000. The first $25,000 reaches every tax, including school taxes, and the added $25,000 applies to assessed value over $50,000 for non-school taxes. After the first year, growth in assessed value is capped at the lower of 3 percent or CPI, which the Department of Revenue prints as 2.7 percent for 2026. A sale resets the property to just value the next January 1.

Renting out the home ends homestead, apart from the servicemember rule in the statutes. Veterans and seniors may qualify for further benefits, and the Charlotte County Property Appraiser is the office that decides each case.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Charlotte County households?
sections.html:
Median household income is $69,952 for 2020 to 2024 in 2024 dollars, and per capita income is $42,592. Median gross rent is $1,464, and monthly owner costs run $1,773 with a mortgage and $678 without one.

Only 43.2% of people aged 16 and over are in the civilian labor force, which fits a county where 40.9% of residents are 65 or older. The county counts 19,280 veterans, 4,601 employer establishments in 2023 and 90,542 households of 2.17 people on average.

For a seller, the ownership numbers matter most. With 87.3% of residents in the same house a year earlier, many owners have held their homes long enough to carry a capped assessment, and a buyer inherits the reset value instead of that cap.

sections.h2: How is the tax handled when you sell in Charlotte County?
sections.html:
The closing agent prorates the year between buyer and seller and pays what is owed from the proceeds, including any delinquent amount.

Get a current payoff from the tax collector at (941) 743-1350 and ask whether a certificate has been sold, because a certificate holder must be paid with interest to clear the lien. The deed itself carries Florida documentary stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 of consideration, paid to the clerk at recording, and all parties to the document are liable.

A buyer of a home that had homestead should expect a bill without the seller's exemption and capped value, because a change of ownership resets the assessment. Ask the appraiser and tax collector for the numbers that apply to your parcel.

faqs.q: Who sends the Charlotte County property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Charlotte County Tax Collector mails it on or before November 1, using the roll certified by the property appraiser. Call (941) 743-1350 with billing questions.

faqs.q: What is the early payment discount in Charlotte County?
faqs.a: It is 4% for payment in November, 3% in December, 2% in January and 1% in February. March payments get no discount, and April 1 is delinquency.

faqs.q: Can Charlotte County taxes be paid in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, if the estimated tax is above $100 and you apply before May 1. Payments are due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31.

faqs.q: How long before a tax certificate becomes a tax deed application?
faqs.a: The holder may apply after two years from the date the tax became delinquent. Certificates last seven years from issuance, and you can redeem before a deed is issued.

faqs.q: Where do I file for homestead in Charlotte County?
faqs.a: File with the Charlotte County Property Appraiser by March 1. The appraiser's office decides eligibility, and the tax collector does not.
